chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali, from one of our companions, from one of them (peace be upon him), who said:
The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) wore Ihram in two cotton cloths.

key_terms.أَحْرَمَ: Entered the state of Ihram (ritual consecration for Hajj or Umrah)
key_terms.كُرُسُفٍ: Cotton fabric (a specific type of fine cotton cloth)

ai.seo_question: What did the Prophet wear for Ihram according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith, transmitted through the chain of the Prophet's companions in *Al-Kafi*, highlights the Prophet's (peace be upon him and his family) practice of entering Ihram in two pieces of *kurusuf* (a fine, thin cotton fabric). In Shia jurisprudence, this serves as a foundational evidence for the peribility of wearing sewn garments or specific textiles during pilgrimage, contrasting with the stricter interpretations that prohibit all sewn clothing, thereby emphasizing the Sunnah's flexibility in ritual attire.
